correctness.rationale: For each length N=2^k>=8, the odd-part rule gives S_N(t)=N/2-1+p_J+p_(J+1), J=ceil(t/(N/2)), so there are at most three ones counts. The complementary values at every pair of consecutive odd indices force the transition count to equal N/2 for matching endpoints and N/2-1 otherwise. Binary two-letter factor counts are then uniquely determined from the ones count and endpoints. For N>=16, j in {1,3,11} and offsets {2,3,4,7} produce every combination; the length-eight base case has twelve explicitly checked starts. The packaged checker tests this logic at dyadic lengths 8 through 4096, but the proof is universal.

value.rationale: At the natural powers-of-two scales of a canonical automatic word, the previously determined one-abelian complexity is exactly three. The theorem supplies an exact all-scale structural refinement: each such class splits into all four possible endpoint states, and pair-count constraints prove no additional classes occur. This complete infinite-family invariant has a direct interpretation in ordered-bigram reconstruction and is not implied by the classical one-abelian recurrence.
